LOWER LIMBS. [33] [Atro. s.]
(In sick :) Continual dragging of legs when assisted, or rather held up, in walking.
(In sick :) Says her "limbs feel like sticks," and thought she could not use them to walk across room to sofa, but with aid she did so with considerable difficulty.
Œdema of legs. θ Albuminuria.
   

LIMBS IN GENERAL. [34] [Atro. s.]
Hands and feet cold and covered with cold sweat. θ Peritonitis.
Upper and lower limbs always cold. θ Gastric disorder.
(In sick :) Numbness and heaviness in her limbs so great that she feared the results of going to sleep lest she should never awaken.
   

REST. POSITION. MOTION. [35] [Atro. s.]
Bending : pain in left ovary better.
(In sick :) Even when supported, could not move a step, feet being too heavy, and feeling no bottom.
   

NERVES. [36] [Atro. s.]
(In sick :) Involuntary movements of hands towards head.
(In sick :) Convulsive trembling of muscles of upper limbs.
Throwing about limbs. θ Puerperal eclampsia.
Different parts affected with spasms.
(In sick :) Subsultus tendinum.
Spasms increased when disturbed ; left to himself they came every two, three minutes.
Convulsions after meningitis spinalis cured by Bellad. ; remaining stiffness of lower limbs cured by Nux vom.
Epilepsy from ovarian irritation.
Some forms of epilepsy and chorea.
(In sick :) Malaise and staggers, lasting more than eight hours.
Staggering, or complete inability to walk.
(In sick :) Great helplessness, amounting to partial paralysis of arms and legs.
(In sick :) Could not rise, felt no bottom under his feet, staggered against the mirror.
Syncope from asthma or shock.
   

SLEEP. [37] [Atro. s.]
Frequently a prolonged yawn when sitting still in a dull apathetic, or drowsy condition.
(In sick :) Restless night, with little sleep.
(In sick :) Broken sleep.
Nights restless, only sleep towards morning. θ Diseased pancreas.
Sleep was much disturbed on account of frequent gastric pains, which often occurred with great violence each night, especially when turning in bed.
(In sick :) At times during night, when nearly lost in sleep, she would suddenly start as if frightened.
Slept pretty well.
Could not be aroused at 6 A. M.
Drowsiness, or somnolency, with tendency to quiet dreams and delirium.
(In sick :) Somnolency with nervous startings.
Comatose, with clonic spasms of biceps flexor cubiti, and muscles of jaw ; limbs cold.
Deep sopor after puerperal eclampsia.
After vigorous efforts to arouse him, signs of consciousness.
   

TIME. [38] [Atro. s.]
Towards morning : sleep.
6 A. M. : could not be aroused.
Morning : illusion of thousand-legged worm on her carpet ; pulse 108.
During day : slight action of bowels.
All day : wakeful and delirious ; passed but little urine.
Between 6 and 7 P. M. : vomiting.
Evening : the eyes of another lady seem to her very large, and she could not avoid looking at them ; diarrhœic stool.
Night : saw numberless white flies on a white door ; thick stool ; restlessness ; gastric pains ; sudden starting when falling asleep.
Between 10 P. M. and 1 A. M. : profuse, frequent urination.
Between 11 P. M. and 1 A. M. : vomiting.
   

TEMPERATURE AND WEATHER. [39] [Atro. s.]
(In sick :) Feels faint and greatly in need of fresh air.
   

FEVER. [40] [Atro. s.]
Slight elevation of temperature of surface, rarely exceeding one degree, still slighter of internal body.
A general diffusion of warmth throughout cutaneous surface.
(In sick :) Dry, hot skin ; 3d day.
Slight sweat.
Typhoid and septic fevers.
   

LOCALITY AND DIRECTION. [42] [Atro. s.]
Right : eye intolerant of light ; pupil contracted ; tumor in side pyloric region ; ache side of head ; gouty affection of wrist.
Left : impaired vision of eye ; pupil increased five times in size : unendurable pains in region below stomach to side ; pain in ovary.
   

SENSATIONS. [43] [Atro. s.]
Violent stitches in base of brain, above eyes and in temples.
Pinching : in stomach.
Burning : in back ; under sternum ; in region of stomach.
Aching : in forehead.
Neuralgia : in ovary.
Sticking, contractive pain : in stomach.
Pressure : under parietal bones ; at stomach.
Fluttering : in cardiac region.
Numbness : in limbs.
Dryness : of mouth ; of tongue ; into pharynx.
Uneasiness : in stomach.
Undefined pain : in and over eyes ; in jaws ; at epigastrium ; in ovary.
   

TISSUES. [44] [Atro. s.]
Hyperæsthesia of some nervous branch of ophthalmic, auditory, olfactory, vagus and plexus solaris, of uterus and sphincter of bladder.
Rheumatic fever.
During last weeks, remarkable wasting. θ Diseased pancreas.
Much emaciated, from a gastric disorder.
Collapse of cholera.
   

TOUCH. PASSIVE MOTION. INJURIES. [45] [Atro. s.]
Deep pressure : pain below stomach < ; abdomen worse.
Touch : tumor in pyloric region sensitive.
   

STAGE OF LIFE, CONSTITUTION. [47] [Atro. s.]
Miss, æt. 24, since 5 years, headache before menses ending with epilepsy.
Blonde, slightly built woman, æt., 25, had three children ; since 5 years ; gastric disorder.
Unmarried woman, æt. 30.
(In sick :) Intelligent married woman, æt. 40, medium size, nervo-sanguine temperament, good health ; poisoned from using locally for toothache.
Unmarried woman, æt. 40, for six years vomiting after eating.
   

RELATIONS. [48] [Atro. s.]
Antidote to Muscarine, or poisoning by mushrooms, especially dyspnœa.
Antidote to meconate of morphia, or any other salt of opium, especially where the heart's action is greatly diminished.
Atrop. sulph. is to be preferred in cases in which Bellad. does not act effectually and permanently.
(In sick :) For hours he was kept constantly on the move, and strong galvanic currents passed along nape of neck every fifteen minutes, irritating him in a great degree.
